description: The LCS of two random strings is equivalent to a last passage percolation (LPP) problem on a grid with Bernoulli weights. For the Bernoulli matching model (independent random matches), the Tracy-Widom distribution governs fluctuations, as shown by Majumdar-Nechaev (2005). Bridging from the exactly solvable Bernoulli model to the true LCS could yield new bounds.
mathematical_formalization: Bernoulli model: w_{ij} ~ Bernoulli(1/k) independently. LPP value T = max over up-right paths of sum w_{ij}. For k=2: E[T]/n -> 2(sqrt(2)-1) ~ 0.8284. True LCS: w_{ij} = 1[x_i=y_j] has correlations. Gap 0.8284 - gamma_2 ~ 0.017 measures correlation effect.
implementation_hypothesis: Develop a coupling between Bernoulli and true LCS models. The coupling inequality gives gamma_2 <= LPP_Bernoulli - correction. Estimate the correction term by measuring covariance structure.
experiment_seed: Simulate both models for n=100,500,1000,5000. Compare means and variances. Difference in means estimates the correlation penalty.
